FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 1) (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Apiary Industry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 


Beehives are kept on stands to protect bee colonies from ants and to protect boxes from termites, etc. Particularly 
while using bee-colonies for pollination of agricultural crops bee colonies are migrated to farms for a short 
duration. Even in their permanent honey-flow sites, bee-colonies are required to be migrated locally for deriving 
maximum benefit of the flora. A portable stand, particularly a folding one, therefore, forms an essential accessory 
of the beehive. 


This standard was first published in 1960 and subsequently revised in 1977 in order to split the standard into two 
parts; Part I Covering requirements for folding type beehive stand and Part 2 Covering the requirements for fixed 
type beehive stand. This revision has been brought out to update the dimensions and figures of folding type 
beehive stand as per the current apiculture practices. Apart from the above, the standard has been brought out in 
the latest style and format of the Indian Standards. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 "Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1735 (Part 1) : 2023 


Indian Standard 


BEEHIVE STAND — SPECIFICATION 
PART 1 FOLDING TYPE 


( Second Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements of folding 
type stand used for keeping beehives in the field. 


2 SIZES 


The sizes of the folding stand should be as shown in 
Fig. 1 and Fig. 2. 


3 MATERIAL 


The folding stand shall be constructed from 
20 mm x 5 mm mild steel strips. Nuts and bolts used 
shall be of the size shown in Fig. 1. The legs shall be 
fitted with suitable iron discs. 


4 CONSTRUCTIOAL DETAILS 


The pieces of the strip should be bent in U-shape as 
per the sizes shown in Fig. 1. Two small pieces of 
strip should be welded at the ends at the distance as 
shown in the figures to the bent strip of shorter 
height so as to bring its total height equal to the taller 
one. A piece of strip should also be welded to the 
legs of the bent strip to keep the legs in position. A 
hole of appropriate size should be drilled exactly in 
the center of the bent strip as well as in the pieces of 
the stripe welded on both the main bent stripe. These 
should then be joined together by bolt and nuts of 
appropriate size. The iron discs should be fitted to 
all the four ends of the stripes. These ends should 
also serve as legs of the stand. 


5 SHAPE AND DESIGN 


The folding stand should be, as far as possible, of the 
shape and dimensions as given in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2. 


6 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


6.1 The stand shall be finished properly. The 
welding shall be satisfactory and the drilling of holes 
shall be exactly in the center of the length of the bent 
stripes. The stand shall be symmetrical on both sides 
and shall stand firm on the ground. 


6.2 The stand should be suitably coated with 
protective paint. 


7 MARKING 


7.1 Each folding beehive stand shall be marked with 
following particulars: 


a) Manufacturer's name and the trade mark; 
b) Yearof manufacture; and 
c) Batch and serial or code number. 


7.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the 
Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
product (s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


All dimension in millimeters. 


FIG. | FOLDING TYPE BEE HIVE STAND WITH DIMENSIONS

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
